title: Macroeconomics, money and banking
audience: a college student in a finance, accounting or business degree program, or a career changer studying the same material on their own
purpose: Measure output, inflation and unemployment; model long-run growth and short-run fluctuations with IS-LM and aggregate demand and supply; explain money creation, central banking, monetary policy tools and the yield curve; and analyze fiscal policy, financial crises and open-economy effects.

weeks.5: The central bank and monetary policy tools
weeks.6: Interest rates and the yield curve
weeks.8: Aggregate demand, aggregate supply and the Phillips curve

blocks.deliverable: Compute real GDP, the GDP deflator and CPI inflation.
Solve for steady state in a Solow model.
Explain the policy rate path and a yield curve shape.
Week 7 midterm; analyze two policy shocks with IS-LM.
Explain a bank run and deposit insurance.
Submit the project; take an unseen 120 minute final in week 14.

project: Policy brief: use FRED data on output, inflation, unemployment and interest rates to assess the current position of the economy, explain the central bank's recent decisions with the course models, and write a three-page brief with charts and a balanced outlook.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
